title: Docker / container runtime crash signals
description: Patterns surfacing container exit codes, OOM kills, runtime exec failures, and panic traces — both from container logs and from docker / containerd / runc output.

patterns.name: non-zero exit code
patterns.explanation: The container process exited with a non-zero status, so the workload did not complete normally.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because the container workload failed and may be unavailable or repeatedly restarting.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Expected command failures and intentionally failing test containers can emit this line.

patterns.name: oom (out of memory)
patterns.explanation: The runtime reports that a container or process exceeded its memory budget.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because memory pressure terminated work and can cascade across a node.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: A deliberately memory-limited benchmark or expected batch peak can cause this signal.

patterns.name: oci runtime exec failed
patterns.explanation: The OCI runtime could not execute a command inside the container.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because runtime execution failed at the container boundary and blocks the requested workload.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: A removed executable, bad image, or a test of failure handling can produce the same message.

examples.positive: OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed

patterns.name: go panic stack
patterns.explanation: A Go process emitted a panic marker, which normally precedes an unrecovered stack trace.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because an unrecovered panic usually terminates the process serving the container.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: A captured panic in a test or deliberately recovered diagnostic can be benign.

examples.positive: panic: runtime error: index out of range

patterns.name: container restarting
patterns.explanation: The container runtime reports a restart, which may be part of recovery or a loop.
patterns.severityRationale: Notice because a restart is an operational signal that needs context but is not by itself a failure.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Rolling deployments and deliberate restarts commonly produce this message.
